text:
maya: CI-nightly popped red on a runtime unit: `serve_retry_ordering_test` failing intermittently in linux-opt. stack looks timing-related, can someone kick a quick rerun and help capture logs? :grimacing:

sam: on it, re-running now. would love a minimal repro if we can get one.

ci-bot: triggered rerun for build 5821 (https://ci.redwood/test/5821). status: started. logs will stream to the run page. :gear:

leo: heads up — last time this failed it ended up being a test seed + timer jitter combo. try `--test_arg=--seed=12345` to force determinism when reproducing locally.

maya: good tip. sam — when ci finishes can you grab the `stderr` and the core test runner flags? also paste the failing assertion snippet if present.

sam: ci finished, still red. attaching tail of failing output:```
E serve_retry_ordering_test.cpp:142: expected 3 retries but got 2
  at runtime/serve/retry_manager.cc:87
  recent events:
    0.003s: call start
    0.150s: prefetched KV
    0.180s: retry scheduled (backoff=50ms)
    0.210s: retry executed
    0.210s: response arrived
```

anya: interesting — response arrived exactly at retry window boundary. could be clock sync in the test harness or the mocked timer resolution.

leo: can we run the test with `--gtest_repeat=50` and `RUNTIME_FAKE_CLOCK=1` to see frequency? on my machine a repeat sweep found it ~1/30.

maya: +1 to sweeping. also add `--test_output=all` so we get the exact timing lines every run.

sam: starting local sweep now: `RUNTIME_FAKE_CLOCK=1 bazel test //runtime/serve:serve_retry_ordering_test --test_output=all --gtest_repeat=50`

deploy-bot: note: there was a small runtime kernel update rolled yesterday to staging that changed internal nanosleep handling. tagging @infra for visibility.

leo: ack. that kernel tweak could change scheduling jitter. if infra confirms, we should pin the test to tolerate +-1 tick or mock the scheduler in the test.

anya: quick suggestion for capture: wrap the failing case with extra debug prints for wall time vs fake clock:
```
LOG("wall=" << now_wall_ms() << " fake=" << fake_clock_ms());
```
That will show if wall time overtakes fake clock at boundary.

sam: sweep results: 50 runs produced 2 failures. logs uploaded to gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/abcd1234 (contains full outputs + flags).

maya: thanks. can someone open a quick bisect job to narrow PR range? if this regressed after the kernel update it might be infra, but could also be a subtle change in retry scheduling.

leo: I'll queue a bisect across the last 12 commits touching `retry_manager` and `serve` with the same test harness. estimated runtime ~2h.

ci-bot: bisect job started: https://ci.redwood/bisect/7921. will post candidate commits as they complete.

anya: meanwhile, to get prod-safe we should add a transient test guard to accept either ordering (2 or 3 retries) while we root cause, and create a follow-up to tighten once fixed. might reduce flaky noise.

maya: agreed on a short-lived guard. please add a comment referencing this thread and the gist. sam can you prepare the PR?

sam: will open PR with guard + expanded logging and link to bisect/gist in description. assigning to @leo for review. ETA 1hr. :thumbsup:

maya: awesome. keep posting updates here and ping if bisect finds a clear culprit. cheers.
